text.en:
Pick almost any 4-digit number, rearrange largest minus smallest digits repeatedly, and wait.
"Why does everyone land on 6174?!" gasped Tara.

Numbers are full of surprising playgrounds! A supercell in a grid is a number bigger than every touching neighbour. A palindrome reads identical forwards and backwards, like 121 or 4554.
Indian mathematician D. R. Kaprekar discovered 6174: take any 4-digit number (not all equal digits), subtract smallest arrangement from largest arrangement, and repeat—you reach 6174 within steps!
And in Collatz steps (halve even numbers, triple-plus-1 odd numbers), chains bounce up and down until landing cleanly at 1!
Maths isn't only sums in notebooks—numbers hide clever puzzles discovered by playful curiosity.
Try a Supercell grid: circle any cell that is strictly greater than all its side-by-side neighbours!
Notice digits tell stories too! How many numbers from 1 to 100 contain the digit 7? Ten in the units place, ten in the 70s, minus double-counted 77 = 19 numbers.
Now test a Palindrome—a number reading the same forwards and backwards, like 121, 585 or clock time 12:21.
Take any 2-digit number like 38, reverse it (83) and add: 38 + 83 = 121—an instant palindrome!
Now meet Maharashtrian teacher D. R. Kaprekar's magic number 6174! Pick 3524 -> biggest 5432 minus smallest 2345 = 3087.
Repeat once more with 3087: 8730 - 0378 = 8352, then 8532 - 2358 = 6174—and 7641 - 1467 locks on 6174 forever!
Next try the Collatz conjecture: start anywhere—if even, divide by 2; if odd, multiply by 3 and add 1.
For example 6 -> 3 -> 10 -> 5 -> 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1! Mathematicians still try to prove every starting number hits 1.
Finally, quick mental estimation—like checking if 4,980 + 3,015 is near 8,000—catches calculator typos in seconds!

problem.en: Apply one Kaprekar step to 2,025 (digits not all the same) and see what number appears next.

text.en: Arrange the digits of 2025 from largest to smallest.
Arrange the digits from smallest to largest.

prompt.en: Why do 4-digit numbers like 4444 fail to reach 6174 in the Kaprekar routine?

commonMisconceptions.en: 6174 works even when all 4 digits match.

points.en: Supercell: larger than all adjacent neighbours.
Palindrome: reads the same forwards and backwards.
Kaprekar's 6174: biggest minus smallest repeats to 6174.
